subject: Transportation Systems
title: Block Signaling
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Block Signaling.

hook.text: Subway trains run in tunnels with no way to see what's ahead. Signals keep them from colliding.

buildup.text: The track is divided into blocks. Only one train can occupy each block at a time.

discovery.text: When a train enters a block, the signal behind it turns red. The next train must wait.

twist.text: Shorter blocks allow trains to run closer together—but require more signals and higher costs.

climax.text: New York still uses a signaling system from the 1930s. Replacing it will take decades.

punchline.text: Old signals work. They just can't run more trains.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of block signaling in a subway?
options: To prevent two trains from occupying the same section
